column1: # Label terms (label-terms/3): the names a United States ingredient statement uses, each with what it tells the diet gate beyond its own words.

# term: the name as read, lower case, singular. kind: food (a single food or a regulated common name), additive (a functional additive, with its INS/E number), flavour (a flavouring or spice term, judged by its own words), composite (a prepared food whose name hides what it is made of; a composite also gives the restriction types that restrict one of its contents a companion pattern, DefaultRestrictionCriteria.CompositeCompanions).

# names: other spellings and numbers, joined by |. contains: what the term is or is made of, as words the restriction patterns read (a major-allergen word is read with every word of its class). may: what it may be made of when the label does not say (held as unknown where a restriction names it). source: why.

# Sources: FALCPA = Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act 201(qq) and 403(w) as amended by the Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act of 2004 and the FASTER Act of 2021 (major food allergens; a major allergen in any ingredient, flavouring, colouring or incidental additive is declared by its source name in the statement or a Contains line, highly refined oils excepted). FDA-QA5 = FDA, Questions and Answers Regarding Food Allergens, edition 5 (2025). 21CFR = Title 21, Code of Federal Regulations (standards of identity; 101.4 and 101.22 for the naming of ingredients, spices and flavourings). INS = Codex Alimentarius, Class Names and the International Numbering System for Food Additives (CAC/GL 36-1989). SR = USDA FoodData Central SR Legacy food description. LABEL = the ingredient statement of the leading brand, as USDA FoodData Central's branded file publishes it. Classic composites whose name does not say what is in them (label-terms/3, staging checkpoint 5) cite public-domain references: ESCOFFIER = A. Escoffier, Le Guide Culinaire (1903; in English A Guide to Modern Cookery, 1907). FARMER = Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896). BEETON = Isabella Beeton, The Book of Household Management (1861). IT-DM-2005 = Italy, Decreto ministeriale 22 luglio 2005 on panettone, pandoro and colomba (the composition the names may be sold under). WIEGAND = E. H. Wiegand, the maraschino process, cherries held in a sulfur dioxide and calcium brine (Oregon Agricultural College, 1925).
